newsitem.title: FRANCE: RALLYING-SUPERB FINISH ALLOWS MCRAE TO WIN TOUR OF CORSICA.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SUPERB FINISH ALLOWS MCRAE TO WIN TOUR OF CORSICA.

text.p: A sensational finish allowed Briton Colin McRae to beat Spaniard Carlos Sainz and win the Tour of Corsica world championship rally on Wednesday.
McRae, who had started the final day of the rally in fourth position overall, 22 seconds behind Sainz, closed the gap to seven seconds with just one timed stage remaining.
The Scot took every conceivable risk in the closing stretch over 34.33 kms from Stiliccione to Marati, in the mountains south of Ajaccio, to drive his Subaru Impreza to victory.

McRae, the 1995 world champion, gained 15 seconds on Sainz's Ford Escort in that stage alone and the Spaniard had to settle for second place overall, eight seconds back, according to unofficial results.
Frenchman Gilles Panizzi, in a two-wheel drive Peugeot 306, came third 38 seconds behind the winner.
In the world championship standings, McRae remained in second place but he is now only two points behind leader Tommi Makinen of Finland.
Makinen, the reigning world champion, crashed out of the Corsica rally when his Mitsubishi Lancer collided with a cow on Tuesday. He has 28 points compared to McRae's 26.
